key_insight: A graph neural network can accurately predict transition-metal adsorption energies on graphene quantum dots, enabling much faster catalyst screening than first-principles calculations.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical surrogate model for rapid discovery and optimization of carbon-based single-atom catalysts, cutting screening cost by about six orders of magnitude versus DFT.
method: Trained a GNN on density functional theory adsorption-energy data.
Used graphene quantum dot structures with transition-metal adsorption configurations as graph inputs.
Learned to predict adsorption energies for fast virtual screening.
evidence_signal: The model achieved R² = 0.906 and MAE = 0.101 eV on evaluation data from the abstract.
watch_item: Performance may depend on how well the training set covers unseen metals, sites, and GQD geometries, so extrapolation beyond the DFT dataset should be treated cautiously.
paper_title: GQD-AdsNet: Graph Neural Networks Unlock Rapid Exploration of Transition Metal Adsorption on Graphene Quantum Dots
